report:
## Conclusion: The claim is false — soursop does not cure cancer in humans.

**What the evidence shows:**

Laboratory (in vitro) and some animal studies have found that compounds in soursop/graviola (Annona muricata), particularly acetogenins, can kill certain cancer cell lines in a petri dish. This is the basis for widespread internet claims that it is "10,000 times more effective than chemotherapy." However, no rigorous human clinical trials have tested soursop as a cancer treatment, and cell-culture results routinely fail to translate into safe, effective human therapies. Fact-checking organizations, oncology sources, and academic reviewers are unanimous that current evidence is insufficient to support a "cure" claim (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/soursop-cancer-cure/; https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2022/sep/27/facebook-posts/fact-checking-claims-tree-fruit-soursop-cures-canc/; https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/meta-programme-fact-checks/no-evidence-soursop-leaf-tea-cures-cancer-depression).

Memorial Sloan Kettering's integrative medicine database explicitly states there is no proof soursop treats cancer in people and flags safety concerns (https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/graviola). Wikipedia's summary, drawing on peer-reviewed sources, echoes this: "there is not enough reliable medical evidence that it is effective for treating cancer" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soursop). Importantly, that same source and MSK note a genuine safety concern: annonacin, a compound in soursop, has been linked in research to neurotoxicity and atypical parkinsonism, particularly with heavy, chronic consumption in the Caribbean.

Some smaller, newer studies (e.g., on prostate biomarkers, safety/tolerability trials) are preliminary, non-definitive, and do not demonstrate a "cure."

**Bottom line:** Your skepticism is well-supported. Soursop shows some anticancer activity in lab settings, but there is no credible human clinical evidence it cures cancer, and relying on it instead of proven treatment could be harmful and even neurotoxic with excessive use.
